name: Idea X-Ray
need: Without it, people burn real money on ideas they never tested — no score, no fixes, no warning before the first dollar.
tesla: The score path — 64 → 71 → 58 — watching your idea get more viable or stay a money trap. A quiz gives you a number; this watches your back for months.
what: Paste any business idea; it grades it 0–100 across 8 real factors, tells you what's strong and what to fix before you spend, and tracks the idea's score trajectory as you learn.

name: Dream Plan Builder
need: Without it, big goals die — no plan, no weekly follow-through, and no idea what to actually do this week.
tesla: The This Week view — type your dream once, and every Sunday the app tells you exactly what this week means. Nobody ever made the one button that runs your whole goal.
what: Type a big goal; get a dated step-by-step plan with phases, budget split, week-by-week actions, and 8 milestones with a live progress bar.

name: Story Spark
need: Without it, parents face the bedtime-story panic every single night — an empty head, and a kid who hates repeats.
tesla: A parent realizing they will never run out of bedtime stories again — fresh, personal, with a lesson, in 5 seconds, plus a library of favorites their kid asks for by name.
what: Original multi-chapter bedtime stories in seconds — your kid as the hero, age-matched wording, your chosen lesson woven into the ending, never repeated.

name: Paycheck Stretch
need: Without it, people run dry mid-cycle and eat overdraft fees.
tesla: The daily number heals itself — overspend today and tomorrow's number drops to absorb it, so one bad day never silently kills the cycle.
what: Turns each paycheck into a day-by-day spending plan: bills first, savings set aside, the rest split across every day until payday — with overdraft warnings before they happen.

name: Bill Oracle
need: Surprise bill weeks are why people fall behind; this kills the surprise.
tesla: It doesn't just show your bills — it names the week that's going to hurt and prices the danger away with one number.
what: Enter your bills once; it forecasts six months ahead, flags the danger weeks, and gives you the exact amount to set aside before each one hits.

name: Eat It First
need: Families throw away roughly $1,500 of food a year because nobody tracks what's about to expire.
tesla: Your fridge becomes a wallet — a personal scoreboard of dollars rescued vs dollars tossed, so saving food feels like making money.
what: Fridge inventory with expiry tracking, a Cook Tonight urgency list, meal plans drafted from what you own, and a running score of money rescued vs wasted.

name: Use What You Have
need: Cooking stalls when people don't know what to do with what's already in the kitchen.
tesla: Every cooking app starts from recipes you pick — this one starts from ingredients you already have and ranks the dinners by coverage.
what: Type in what's in your kitchen and get real dinners ranked by how much of your exact pantry they use — a saved pantry feeds the engine every night.

name: Day Reset
need: Mornings get lost to deciding — the first hour of every day burns on choosing what to do first.
tesla: Every planner makes you plan in the morning, foggy and behind — this closes the day at night, so you never decide before coffee.
what: A 60-second nightly close-out: carry over what's left, set tomorrow's priorities, and wake up to a day that's already decided.

name: Today Card
need: Every morning asks the same three questions — what's due, what's left, what's next — and people open five apps to answer them.
tesla: One card answers all three questions and picks the one thing to hit first — after that, the five-app morning looks ridiculous.
what: One morning card: bills due today and this week, money left, and the single next move — all three answers on one screen.

name: Wear Log
need: Everyone decides what's dirty by the sniff test — a guess dressed up as a habit.
tesla: The basket fills itself the moment a shirt hits its wear limit, and the forecast names laundry day before you run out of clean clothes.
what: Tracks every garment by wear count, knows what's dirty without you remembering, and forecasts laundry day from your actual rotation.

name: Chore Court
need: Chore fights are relationship fights — and they're unfixable because nobody can measure the unfairness.
tesla: Every chore gets a price tag — households balance budgets to the penny but split chores by vibes; this makes the split arithmetic, with the proof on screen.
what: Set up your household once; the fairness engine prices every chore in effort points, assigns and auto-rotates them, and issues THE RULING when someone disputes the split.

name: Receipt Bank
need: Money leaks out unnoticed — nobody overspends on one big thing; they slowly pay more for the same life.
tesla: Your bank app shows what you spent — this names the exact dollars leaking out as your costs creep up each month. Once you see that number, you can't unsee it.
what: A creep detector, not an expense tracker: log receipts and it flags quietly rising costs with a Leak Index — the share of your spending that's pure price creep.

name: Pill Diary
need: Nobody can tell from memory at 8:12 PM whether the 8:00 dose went down.
tesla: Every reminder app pretends it can remind you — this one does the honest thing instead, and turns your own log into analytics and a doctor-ready report.
what: An honest medication diary — a diary, not an alarm: tap Taken or Skipped per dose, see today's status instantly, with 30/90-day adherence stats and copyable doctor-visit reports.
